newsitem.title: POLAND: GERMAN BERLINER GETS POLISH BANKING LICENCE.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN BERLINER GETS POLISH BANKING LICENCE.

text.p: Berliner Bank AG, a part of the German holding Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG, got a licence from the Polish central bank to operate in Poland under the name of Berliner Bank (Poland) SA, the bank said in a statement.
It said the Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG bought a stake in the small Polish Polsko-Kanadyjski Bank Sw. Stanislawa SA in Warsaw (Pol-Can-Bank) before receiving the licence.
The fully-owned Polish subsidiary of Berliner will be based in Warsaw with a share capital of 30 million zlotys and employ a total of 40 staff in Wrasaw and a Poznan branch.
It will start operating in the first half of 1997.
The statement said the bank eyed Poland as the biggest German trade partner in Eastern Europe and will focus on servicing medium-sized corporates, financial institutions and chosen individuals.
"The bank wants to contribute to the development of the Polish economy by financing investment and infrastructure projects," it said.
From 1994 the bank has had a representative office in Poznan.
